claim: LLM-generated research ideas are rated more novel than expert human ideas at ideation (novelty 4.84 human, 5.64 AI, 5.81 AI plus human rerank; 49 ideas per arm, 79 reviewers, 298 reviews) with no significant feasibility loss.
agent_test: Generate ideas with and without a scaffold step at equal tokens; blind-rate novelty and feasibility with a fixed rubric. (Three evidence lines, one underlying study.)

claim: The novelty advantage does not survive execution: after experiments are run, AI ideas drop 1.98 overall points (5.382 to 3.406) vs 0.63 for human ideas (4.596 to 3.968), and the ranking flips.
agent_test: Score ideas before and after a small executed test; measure the gap per arm. Only one study group so far.

claim: LLM judges cannot reliably pick the better research idea: judge accuracy 43.3 to 53.3% vs human inter-reviewer agreement 56.1%, near chance on a balanced task. New: off-the-shelf o3 and GPT-4.1 are near 50% on predicting which idea works (51.9%); expert majority 48.9%; best annotator per topic 60.0%. Above 60% needed fine-tuning on 6,000 outcome pairs (77%) or a data-based validation shown to the judge (Claude 69.0 to 78.9 on a reference-based ranking test).
agent_test: Use the agent as its own judge on a held-out ranked set; compare with chance. Treat self-ranking as weak evidence.

claim: Sampling many LLM ideas collapses into few distinct ones: about 200 non-duplicates of 4000 seed ideas (about 5%, cosine over 0.8); ideas are also similar across runs and models.
agent_test: Measure embedding-duplicate rate of n parallel drafts at equal tokens; test forced-diversity prompts against plain resampling.

claim: Search plus simple physics-inspired tests (symmetry, separability) solves the clean Feynman set: AI Feynman 100/100 vs 71/100 prior; AI Feynman 2.0 solves 73/100 at noise 10^-1.
agent_test: Give the agent a symbolic-regression task with decomposition tests vs none, at equal tokens. (Both papers are by the same group.)

claim: The AI Feynman lead shrinks and depends on noise in an independent benchmark: AIFeynman exact recovery 53% with no noise, but DSR, gplearn and AFP recover more equations above noise 0.01.
agent_test: Run the same task at 0 and 1-10% noise; report exact-solve rate per level.

claim: Putting an LLM inside the evolutionary loop raises equation recovery: LLM-SR beat baselines that ran 2M+ iterations with about 2.5K; LaSR solves 66 to 72 of 100 vs 59 for PySR (abstract says 66, table lists up to 72).
agent_test: Loop: propose a form, fit constants with a tool, feed back error; compare to one-shot proposals at equal tokens.

claim: Gains on famous equations are partly memory: on memorization-resistant problems the best system reaches only 31.5% (Transform) and 28.1% (Synth) symbolic accuracy. New: the feedback loop is a large gain over bare prompting on numeric fit (LLM-SR SA 31.53 vs direct prompt 7.21 on LSR-Transform), LaSR beats PySR on 41 synthetic equations (R2 0.913 vs 0.070) but recovers no true forms, and removing the data-analysis tool in SR-Scientist drops Acc0.01 from 63.57 to 35.66.
schema_part: G do not confuse recall with discovery
agent_test: Test the agent on altered or synthetic versions of known laws; compare with the original versions.

claim: Foundation models can fit trajectories almost perfectly (R2 above 0.9999) while implying inconsistent force laws, so fit quality does not show law discovery.
schema_part: G running check on mechanism not fit
agent_test: Check the agent's proposed law on a shifted data slice, not only on training fit.

claim: End-to-end automated paper pipelines are fragile: an independent test of the AI Scientist found 5 of 12 experiments (42%) failed from coding errors, 4 of 7 papers (57%) had missing figures, 4 of 7 had wrong or invented numbers; median 5 citations, 5 of 34 from 2020 or later. The original paper also shows many ideas dropped at the experiment stage. New: in controlled tests, Agent Laboratory picked one of the first four listed benchmarks in 82.4% of 945 runs, and both systems sometimes used undisclosed subsets or synthetic data.
agent_test: Add a numbers-trace check (every reported number tied to a logged run); count unsupported numbers with and without it.

claim: Self-reported discovery claims are less reliable than computed ones: Kosmos statements were 85.5% accurate for data analysis, 82.1% for literature, 57.9% for synthesis/interpretation (79.4% overall of 102 statements).
agent_test: Tag each agent statement as observed, computed or interpreted; audit accuracy per tag.

claim: Automated novelty checks are over-generous: 49 of 51 AI Scientist ideas were flagged novel, yet experts found 24% of 50 LLM research documents plagiarised (paraphrase or heavy borrowing); automated detectors score about 0 to 1.3% without retrieval.
agent_test: Check novelty claims by retrieval against a corpus; compare self-judged vs retrieval-judged novelty.

claim: Agents in open-ended discovery tasks fall far below humans: DiscoveryWorld best agent 38% easy and 18% challenge vs humans 66%; DiscoveryBench best 25%; ScienceAgentBench best 32.4% (42.2% with o1 at over 10x cost).
agent_test: Run a small DiscoveryWorld-like task suite; compare scaffold vs plain at equal tokens.

claim: Hypothesis generation guided by data and a candidate bank beats few-shot prompting (+31.7%, +13.9%, +3.3%, +24.9% on four datasets) and can beat supervised learning by about 12% on two hard sets. Boundary: on HypoBench synthetic tasks recovery falls from 93.8% to 38.8% as difficulty rises; no open-ended unlabelled test exists.
schema_part: O hypothesis bank updated on failures
agent_test: Keep a hypothesis bank updated on errors vs none; same token budget.

claim: Zero-shot LLM hypothesis proposers are weakly novel (GPT-3.5 novelty 1.42); adding similar few-shot examples did not raise novelty (1.02), suggesting anchoring.
agent_test: Test whether adding examples to the prompt narrows novelty.

claim: Retrieval of inspirations works on small candidate pools but degrades at fine selection: MOOSE-Chem hit ratio 96% at top 20% falls to 47-52% at top 0.016%; extra screening rounds can lower recall (98.0% to 56.5%).
agent_test: Test staged filtering vs single-pass retrieval at equal tokens.

claim: Multi-agent generate-debate-evolve loops improve quality on the system's own metrics (evolution agent: GPQA precision 70.9 to 75.4%, hypothesis quality 4.7 to 5.6), but the evidence is internal and self-scored.
agent_test: Replicate with blind external scoring.

claim: Replicating papers from scratch is hard: best agent 21.0% on PaperBench; on a 3-paper subset humans 41.4% vs o1 26.6%; an iterative scaffold raised o1 to 43.4% on one variant but hurt Claude 3.5 Sonnet, so scaffold effect is model-dependent.
agent_test: Test whether a verify-then-continue scaffold helps this model, since results are model-dependent.

claim: Early rule-based systems (BACON) re-created a dozen or more historical discoveries from clean, pre-selected tables (Simon 1995, a BACON co-author); 4 of 14 college students rediscovered Kepler's third law in the lab study (Qin and Simon 1990, count via Simon 1995). BACON.6 gets noise robustness by design: data only tests hypotheses, never generates them. Exact law lists and measured noise tolerances were not verified from the 1987 book.
agent_test: Not testable directly; use as boundary note: success depended on supplied variables.

claim: An LLM reviewer matches human reviewers on balanced accuracy (0.65 vs 0.66) but is more over-optimistic (false positive rate 0.31 vs 0.17).
agent_test: Compare the agent's accept/reject calls against known outcomes; tune threshold.

claim: Removing the iterative refinement loop from LLM-SR raises error (NMSE 0.101 in-domain, 0.181 out-of-domain); removing skeleton plus optimizer is worse (0.378 / 0.375). The running check carries real weight.
agent_test: Ablate the feedback step in the agent's loop at equal tokens.

claim: Closed-loop evolutionary code search with an automatic evaluator produces verified new results: AlphaEvolve matched best known on 75% and surpassed on 20% of 50+ open problems (kissing number in 11 dimensions raised to 593). Boundary: the authors also report a cheating phenomenon (leaky verifiers, gamed cheap-LLM oracle) and failure on problems without a smooth score.
agent_test: Use tasks with a programmatic scorer; compare evolve-loop vs best-of-n at equal tokens.

claim: A cheap executed check before ranking moves what it can measure: with a data-based validation shown to the judge, ranking accuracy rose (Gemini 56.9 to 62.3, Claude 69.0 to 78.9). In a human test of top-5 picks, validation won on feasibility (40.0 vs 26.7 loss, p=0.03) and expected effectiveness (43.3 vs 29.2, p=0.02) but not overall (p=0.29). Domain: social science, 8 source papers.
schema_part: G running check / verify state before rank
agent_test: Run a small computed test per candidate idea, then rank; compare with ranking alone at equal tokens, per axis.

claim: Execution feedback inside the loop works when the task is code-checkable: an automated executor ran a large share of LLM ideas (42% to 78% execution rate across ideator/executor pairs), best-of-50 beat the baseline (60.4% vs 48.0%) and evolutionary search reached 69.4%, but RL on the same reward collapsed to a few simple ideas.
schema_part: O propose, evaluate, evolve; keep diversity
agent_test: Pair the check with a diversity or novelty term; count distinct ideas that pass.

claim: Retrieval-grounded novelty checking only works when staged: a retrieve then facet-rerank pipeline flagged 89.66% of known non-novel ideas, while keyword-only retrieval flagged 5.17% and snippet-only 8.62% (58 ideas). With search, the co-scientist reflection agent scored known ideas 2.38 vs 6.14 novelty without search. Token cost and effect on the 24% plagiarism rate not measured.
schema_part: G novelty is checked against sources
agent_test: Run the same ideas through a one-query check and a staged check; count false 'novel' flags.

claim: Evolve loops fail or are gamed when the evaluator is leaky or noisy: AlphaEvolve found loopholes in discrete verifiers and trained its program to extract the hidden answer from a cheap LLM oracle; a yes/no restriction still left noisy answers. Mixed cheap and strong models sometimes beat strong-only runs.
schema_part: G evaluator the generator cannot see or influence
agent_test: Hide the judge prompt and restrict its output; compare proposals against a leaky and a sealed judge.

claim: Process failures of AI scientist systems are mostly silent choices, not code errors: 82.4% positional benchmark choice, undisclosed subsampled or invented datasets, and an auditor reading only the paper detects them at 55% vs 82% with logs and code.
schema_part: G trace log and stated deviations
agent_test: Have the verify step read the full work trace; count deviations caught against the paper alone.
